source: NCERT Class XI, India Physical Environment, Ch. 2 (Structure and Physiography).

sections.heading: 1. Geological Structure
points: India has three geological divisions: the **Peninsular block** (oldest, stable — Archaean gneiss/granite), the **Himalayas and other Peninsular mountains** (young, unstable), and the **Indo-Ganga-Brahmaputra plain** (recent alluvium).
The **Peninsular Plateau** is part of the ancient **Gondwana land** (very old, rigid).

sections.heading: 2. Major Physiographic Divisions
points: India is divided into: **(1) The Northern and North-eastern Mountains, (2) The Northern Plain, (3) The Peninsular Plateau, (4) The Indian Desert, (5) The Coastal Plains, (6) The Islands.**

sections.heading: 3. The Himalayas and Northern Plains

sub: **Greater Himalayas (Himadri)** — highest, permanent snow, Mt Everest/Kanchenjunga.
**Lesser Himalayas (Himachal)** — hill stations (Shimla, Mussoorie), valleys (Kashmir, Kangra).
**Shiwaliks (outer)** — lowest; **Duns** (Dehra Dun) between Shiwaliks and Lesser Himalayas.

points: **Northern Plain** — formed by alluvium of the Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra; divided into **Bhabar, Terai, Bhangar (old alluvium), Khadar (new alluvium)**.

sections.heading: 4. Plateau, Coasts and Islands
points: **Peninsular Plateau** — Central Highlands (Malwa, Bundelkhand) and the **Deccan Plateau**; bordered by the **Western Ghats (Sahyadri)** and **Eastern Ghats**; the Western Ghats are higher/continuous (**Anai Mudi** = highest peak of peninsular India).
**Coastal Plains** — Western (Konkan, Kanara, Malabar — narrow) and Eastern (Northern Circar, Coromandel — broad, deltas).
**Islands** — **Andaman & Nicobar** (Bay of Bengal, volcanic/tectonic — Barren Island = only active volcano) and **Lakshadweep** (Arabian Sea, coral).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Six physiographic divisions: N mountains, N plain, Peninsular plateau, desert, coasts, islands.
Himalayan ranges: Himadri (Greater), Himachal (Lesser), Shiwaliks (Outer); Duns between.
N. Plain zones: Bhabar, Terai, Bhangar (old), Khadar (new).
Western Ghats (Sahyadri) higher/continuous; Anai Mudi = highest peak of South India.
Andaman & Nicobar (volcanic; Barren Island active); Lakshadweep (coral).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Western Ghats are continuous and higher** than the broken Eastern Ghats.
**Barren Island (Andaman)** is India's only active volcano; **Lakshadweep = coral** islands.
